$comment: CANONICAL ADDRESS REGISTRY — the one place every Tegridy address is written down in full.
WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 an operator wallet holding 0.496 SOL nearly could not be found,
because it had only ever been recorded in a session note as a TRUNCATED string ('5hNA2MXk…927v').
Worse, a later session INVENTED a full address to fit that truncation — 45 characters decoding to
33 bytes, not a valid Solana pubkey at all. Had anyone funded it, the money would have been gone.
THE RULES THIS FILE ENFORCES (see verify-addresses.mjs, which fails CI on each):
1. Addresses are stored in FULL. Never a '…', never a '0x1234…abcd' shorthand.
2. Every address is structurally validated — EVM to EIP-55 checksum, Solana to exactly 32 bytes.
3. Nothing in this file may collide with the denylist below.
4. Every non-zero address literal in src/lib/constants.ts AND in src/lib/yield/protocols.ts
must appear here, so an address cannot enter the codebase without being registered and
explained. The rule names files, and the files it names are the whole of its reach: a file
carrying live mainnet addresses that is not named here is not clean, it is unlooked-at.
protocols.ts was exactly that until 2026-09-03 — twenty-seven third-party mainnet addresses,
seven of them the destination of a real deposit from /yield, none of them in constants.ts,
all of them passing a check that had never opened the file.
5. Every contract this repo has actually CREATED on mainnet — read out of the Foundry
broadcast receipts, not out of the source — must appear here or in 'retiredDeploys'.
WHY RULE 5 EXISTS. Rule 4 alone is one-directional: it walks the files it was told to open and
asks the registry about each address it finds. Anything the frontend never names is INVISIBLE
to it, so is anything in a file the list forgot, and so is
anything written in a shape its regex does not match. Both holes were live. Seven live mainnet
contracts sat unregistered underneath a green CI: the four DELEGATECALL libraries linked into
TegridyStaking / TegridyFactory / SwapFeeRouter, the JBAC vault, and the two retired staking
deployments that still custody user positions. A guard that can only ever discover addresses the
frontend already imports cannot notice a missing entry, which is the one thing it was for.
SOLANA CLOSURE IS NOT VISIBLE FROM THE PROGRAM ACCOUNT. `solana program close` deletes the
ProgramData account and leaves the program stub executable-flagged, so `expect.type: executable`
keeps passing for a program that can never run again. Any program id whose closure this registry
asserts must therefore ALSO carry its ProgramData address as its own entry with
`expect.type: absent`, which verify-addresses.mjs enforces unconditionally. Without that second
entry the closure is a sentence; with it, CI reads the chain.
WHAT MUST NEVER GO IN THIS FILE: private keys, seed phrases, or the FILESYSTEM PATHS of keyfiles.
This repository is PUBLIC. Key custody is tracked in an operator-local file that is not committed;
the 'custody' field here says WHO controls a key, never WHERE it is stored.

solana.correction: This entry used to read 'Squads vault PDA index 0 = cp-swap admin::ID and create_support_mint_associated_owner::ID'. Both halves were wrong, and it is the exact confusion that bricked graduation. (a) The cp-swap binary that WAS deployed baked the MULTISIG account EVGSnRZ… as admin::ID — a 495-byte Squads-program-owned account that can neither sign (v4 signs CPIs as the vault) nor be debited by the System Program, and `CreateAmmConfig` has `payer = owner`. create_amm_config was therefore uncallable and migrate_to_amm never got past AmmNotConfigured (6015). (b) The SOURCE fix (#281) repoints admin::ID at deploy-authority Dcjink4RG…, a plain system-owned wallet — still not this vault. (c) create_support_mint_associated_owner::ID is deliberately the multisig, left as-is because it is a pure OR-fallback. This correction is now history rather than a live hazard: both program ids were closed on 2026-08-13, `verify-program-constants.mjs --deployed` has no bytecode left to search, and the question it settled must be re-answered against whatever binary a restart actually deploys.

cp-swap create_pool_fee_reveiver::ID on the `--features devnet` arm — the devnet admin's WSOL ATA. Registered so verify-program-constants can carry it as a FORBIDDEN key: baked into a mainnet binary, every pool-creation fee is paid to an account that does not exist on mainnet.

The throwaway in tegridy-launch's declare_id! (lib.rs:114) AND in deployer::ID's devnet arm (lib.rs:140). Still what trunk compiles against; the mainnet id CpFnacrAC… is patched in at build time per MAINNET_RUNBOOK §5b and never committed. One key, two constants — which is why a byte search of the binary can report it present but cannot say which of the two it came from.

ethereum.$comment: ── /yield: the eight third-party DeFi protocols the surface reads, plus the seven canonical permissionless deposits it wires. None of these is ours, and one of them is where a visitor’s ETH goes when they press a button, so an address remembered slightly wrong is money handed to a stranger. They all live in frontend/src/lib/yield/protocols.ts — a file check 5 did NOT scan until this change, which is exactly the one-directional hole rule 4 exists to warn about, with live mainnet addresses on the wrong side of it. Check 5 now walks protocols.ts as well as constants.ts, so every one of these must stay registered. Each `evidence` line below is the verbatim output of frontend/scripts/verify-yield-protocols.mjs at mainnet block 25893998 (2026-09-03 UTC), which sees bytecode AND reads a canonical view off each address — symbol(), description(), asset(), baseToken(), eETH(), ezETH(), getPool(), getChainId() — so identity here is read, never remembered. That run’s only failures were HTTP 429 from GeckoTerminal on an off-chain market-depth lookup, which touches none of these addresses; every on-chain read passed.

This is NOT documentation and nothing here should be used. It exists so rule 5 has a CLOSED
WORLD: verify-addresses walks every CREATE/CREATE2 in contracts/broadcast/**/1/run-latest.json
and demands each address be either a live registry entry above, denylisted, or listed here.
A new mainnet deploy therefore lands in a broadcast receipt, matches nothing, and FAILS CI
until a human classifies it. That is the failure the one-directional guard could not produce.
Derived from the receipts, so 'script' and 'contract' are what Foundry recorded, not a claim
about what the bytecode does today. Several are superseded by an entry in `ethereum` above —
the constants.ts comments carry the specific 'Prev:' pairings. Some still hold dust or stale
state; none is wired into the frontend.
Adding a row here is a deliberate act of retirement. Never add one to silence CI.
